confirmed_finding.summary: The simulation update rate is coupled to rendering and drops below the requested Growth Speed when rendering falls below 20 FPS.
mechanism: Elapsed time is limited to 0.05 seconds per accepted render.
At a requested Growth Speed of 30, this adds at most 1.5 simulation steps per rendered frame.
The accumulator is capped at 2 steps, and the last-tick timestamp moves forward, discarding the excess elapsed time.
confirmed_finding.clock_probe: Actual NeuralGrowthModel.render() exercised with an injected no-op runtime and deterministic timestamps; it isolates scheduler behavior from GPU speed.
confirmed_finding.history: The same 50ms clamp and two-step accumulator cap are present in ac5e8b2, before the snapshot. This is a confirmed slowdown amplifier, not a proven explanation for the new render-performance regression.

runtime_comparison.conclusion: The controlled runtime test did not reproduce a meaningful current-versus-previous slowdown with Dream Guidance off. The output drawing cost rose about 16x from 384px to 1536px in this software-rendered environment.
limits: The browser selected SwiftShader software WebGL. These absolute frame times are not measurements of the user hardware GPU.
This is an isolated runtime comparison, not a full before/after UI profile.
No GPU timer query extension was available. The raw stepCpuSubmissionOnly samples do not measure completed GPU work.
The initiating cause of the reported new slowdown is not established; the clock finding explains its effect on growth speed.

second_opinion_questions: Is the intended slow-frame policy to preserve real-time simulation speed or deliberately reduce the simulation rate under load?
